items.title: v0.42.1 — fix component resolution in `from_pretrained` to prevent `trust_remote_code` bypass
items.abstract_or_text: This is a security release. See [GHSA-4prv-5hj7-c2xr](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/security/advisories/GHSA-4prv-5hj7-c2xr) for details. This patch release fixes how a component's declared library name is resolved when loading with `from_pretrained`. Pipelines and models declare each component as a `[" ", " "]` pair in `model_index.json` / `config.json`. This release changes how that library name is resolved across the `DiffusionPipeline`, `AutoModel`, and `ModularPipeline` loading paths, and adds a clearer error when the declared class is not found in the resolved module. All users on 0.42.0 are encouraged to upgrade: ``` pip install diffusers==0.42.1 ```

items.title: v0.40.12
items.abstract_or_text: ## Liquid AI LFM3 [LFM3](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3) is Liquid AI's new family of small models built for local agents, tool calling, and structured output, on Liquid's new tri-hybrid architecture. The family includes: - [lfm3](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3): a 1.7B text model with a 256K-token context window - [lfm3-vl](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3-vl): adds image understanding - [lfm3-audio](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3-audio): speech recognition, translation, and text-to-speech in 18 languages - [lfm3-omni](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3-omni): text, images, and audio in one model ```sh ollama run lfm3 ``` ## d1 decision models Liquid AI's d1 models now come in a 2B size, built on LFM3. [d1](https://ollama.com/library/d1) makes decisions about text and images, and [d1-omni](https://ollama.com/library/d1-omni) adds audio. ```sh ollama run d1:2b "I was charged twice for order 4417." --ask "Is this a billing issue?" ``` Note: lfm3 and d1 2b are supported on Apple hardware in this release. Support for Linux/Windows coming soon. ## What's Changed - Faster prompt processing on Apple silicon for Gemma 4, Flint and Laguna models - Speculative decoding now supports DFlash2 draft models on MLX - Gemma 4 keeps more detail in small images - `ollama launch` now works with OpenCode v2 - Fixed tool-only assistant turns from Kimi CLI - Updated MLX and llama.cpp **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.11...v0.40.12

items.abstract_or_text: server: add router device memory margin parameter for dynamic unloading (#21231) * server: add --models-memory-max parameter to allow dynamically unloading models when they exceed a memory size threshold estimate with to-be-loaded model size included use no_alloc to get memory requirements for model load only set model memory_mb if not previously calculated use memory margin instead of total size limit, apply to each device separately add server memory debug logging move llama_context_device_memory function to llama-ext.h fix model count exceeded check improve memory_per_device map naming improve variable naming, fix style also strip models memory margin from child processes cont : clean-up replace device memory map with buft memory map. Use llama_get_memory_breakdown extract duplicated check into helper function move model memory estimation to subprocess precompute name->buft map, map GPU host types to CPU buft cleanup unused variable remove duplicated init calls * adapt to upstream changes * wip * common_memory_reports internface * SERVER_ROLE_MEASURE * server-models-sched * fix build * server : fix memory accounting of measure children and claim spin A measure child runs no_alloc, so the free memory it reports does not include its estimate: subtracting self there erased the memory held by other processes, down to zero with --fit on, and the next load could overshoot the margin. Subtract self only for instance reports. A queued load only checked --models-max before claiming, so when the memory margin blocked it behind a busy model, load() threw and the waiter retried in a tight loop. Refuse the claim while the limits are exceeded and no idle model can be unloaded, so the waiter sleeps on the condition variable until one goes idle. --------- Co-authored-by: Xuan Son Nguyen Co-authored-by: Pascal **Website:** - items.abstract_or_text: model: Add MiniCPM-OCR-Jev (#30980) * model : add MiniCPM-OCR-Jev support The model is a Qwen3.5-VL trunk with a value head read at the last token: it scores an OCR text against an image rendered from it, it does not generate. Add the openbmb-minicpm-ocr-jev decision type, served by POST /v1/systemone. The class scores are the pooled output of the sequence, read with last pooling, so the conversion turns score.weight into cls.output and sets embedding_length_out. The checkpoint has no LM head, so text generation is rejected instead of using the output weights duplicated from the token embeddings. The task is fixed, so its prompt is entirely in the systemone template, the same way h2o-lightning keeps its default there. The processor of the checkpoint allows up to 16384 merged tokens per image, more than the Qwen-VL default of mtmd, so the mmproj keeps the image budget of the preprocessor config. The checkpoint declares MiniCPMOCRForSequenceClassification in its config.json, as other models do. items.abstract_or_text: ggml : relax scale to non-contiguous views (#31146) * ggml : relax scale to non-contiguous views SCALE requires src0 to be 1D-contiguous. Relax this to dim-0 contiguity with arbitrary row strides (ggml_is_contiguous_rows), same as the unary ops in the Metal backend. - ggml: relax the assert in ggml_scale_impl - cpu: address src0 rows through their byte strides (f32, bf16) - cuda: stride-aware kernel, fastdiv row decomposition - metal: support bf16 scale (guarded unary instantiations) - sycl: keep the gate at contiguous, the kernel is flat f32 Add view variants to test_scale. Verified on CPU, Metal and CUDA. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB) * cuda : skip the softcap fusion on non-contiguous views The fused softcap kernel reads src and writes dst as dense arrays, so a view reaching SCALE -> TANH -> SCALE now that SCALE accepts non-contiguous rows would be read wrongly. items.abstract_or_text: tests : fix multi-seq split replay and partial-state cases for trained models (#31216) * tests : fix multi-seq split replay against trained models The rollback snapshot is captured by the graph that decoded the rolled-back tail, while the reference context decodes the same prefix with different batch shapes. The two states differ in the last bits and trained models amplify the difference with every replayed token. Compare only the first replayed token of each seq, then restore the rollback state into the reference context before the seq-1-only tail. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB) * tests : require bit-exact seq-1 isolation in split replay The seq state save is not always bit-lossless - SWA-masked cells are not saved - so reload the restored state back into the rollback context. That way both contexts enter the seq-1-only tail with byte-identical memory, including the cell layout, and the tail logits must match bit-exact. Also assert that the restored state round-trips bit-identical. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB) * tests : drop the n_swa partial-state check from ps The check keys off llama_model_n_swa(), which returns 0 for dsv4 even though its raw KV cache has a 128-cell sliding window. The partial state grows with the tokens there by design, so the flatness check is wrong. Keep the partial **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11922/llama-b11922-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) - items.abstract_or_text: ggml-cpu : rewrite concat as one row kernel for all types (#31179) Every dst row comes from src0 or src1, or for dim 0 from the row of src0 followed by the row of src1, so a single kernel covers every type: a dense source row is one memcpy, quantized types included, and a strided source is copied element by element with the element size known at compile time. Rows are split across threads instead of i2 alone, which is often 1, and are copied in tiles of 32: for a transposed source the elements are walked in the outer loop, so the rows of a tile read neighboring addresses instead of jumping a full row stride per element. items.abstract_or_text: common: pin model resolution on real HF repo layouts (#30548) * tests: pin model resolution on real repo listings Extend test-model-resolution with 63 repo listings captured verbatim from the HF API, chosen to cover every file naming pattern found across 1237 GGUF repos of the major publishers and pruned to whole quant groups. Each repo pins its resolved plans and its cache listing. The expectations follow what each file really is per its GGUF header, not what the current resolver picks, so a mismatch is a resolution bug. Mismatches are collected and reported together before the test fails. * tests: leave the listing unchecked on paths the filesystem refuses Some real split names (DevQuasar's Model.Q2_K.gguf-00001-of-00012.gguf under a quant folder) exceed MAX_PATH once materialized in the temporary cache on Windows, so the listing of such a repo is skipped with a note while its plans stay checked. * tests: pin real listings to master on GGUF convention names only Replace the real repo table with 171 HF listings whose file names follow the GGUF naming convention (lowercase sidecar prefix, - delimited components, quant last), one per layout pattern found across 1174 GGUF repos and pruned to whole quant groups. Repos outside the convention are dropped. Each repo pins the plans and the cache listing master gives today, so the test is a pure harness: any change in resolution shows up here, and mismatches are reported together. **Website:** - **Attestations:** -
